Section 10(43) exempts periodic loan installments, while Section 45 triggers capital gains tax when the bank alienates the property for recovery.
source_provision:
### Reverse Mortgage Scheme: Statutory Framework

| Transaction Stage | Statutory Provision | Tax Treatment | Legal Impact |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Mortgaging Property** | Section 47(xvi) | Not a Transfer | No Capital Gains tax liability at the time of mortgage |
| **2. Receipt of Loan** | Section 10(43) | Fully Exempt | Loan amounts (lump sum or installment) excluded from Total Income |
| **3. Alienation by Bank** | Section 45 | Taxable Transfer | Capital Gains tax triggered upon sale of property for loan recovery |


#### Key Statutory Rules

* **Exemption from Definition of Transfer**: Any transfer of a Capital Asset in a transaction of reverse mortgage under a scheme notified by the Central Government is excluded from Section 2(47).
* **Exemption of Loan Receipts**: Lump sum or periodic monthly disbursements received by an individual borrower under a notified Reverse Mortgage Scheme are completely exempt under Section 10(43).
* **Eventual Alienation**: Taxability arises only when the lender bank alienates or sells the property to recover the outstanding loan and interest.


> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Statutory Distinction:** Mortgage creation and receipt of loan payments are completely tax-exempt during the owner's lifetime. Capital Gains tax liability is deferred until actual alienation of the property by the bank.

director.justification: The tax mechanism excludes reverse mortgage transactions from transfer under Section 47(xvi) and exempts loan payments under Section 10(43), until property alienation triggers Section 45.
director.visual_metaphor: A three-stage tax shield timeline showing non-transfer mortgage creation, exempt installment stream, and ultimate bank recovery sale.
